slides.title: Andrej Karpathy Interview Code Agents, AutoResearch, and the
slides.text: Andrej Karpathy Interview Code Agents, AutoResearch, and the Loopy Era of AI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kwSVtQ7dziU In this episode of the No Priors podcast, Andrej Karpathy discusses the transition from manual coding to the "agentic era." He describes a state of "AI psychosis," where he now spends his time delegating high-level intent to autonomous agents rather than writing lines of code. AutoResearch : Karpathy introduces his project where agents autonomously design and run AI experiments, finding optimizations that human researchers - overlook. The "Claw" Concept: He describes persistent, looping agent harnesses that manage complex tasks, such as his "Dobby" agent that hacked and unified his entire smart home system. Future of Work: Karpathy envisions a "swarm" of untrusted global compute collaborating on research , suggesting that while the digital world will transform at light speed, physical robotics will lag due to the complexity of "atoms." Education: He predicts a shift where humans explain concepts to agents , which then provide personalized, infinitely patient tutoring to students.

slides.title: Anthropic Claude Code Channels Anthropic Claude Code Channels
slides.text: Anthropic Claude Code Channels Anthropic Claude Code Channels (in "Research") Use Telegram or Discord to interact with Claude Code AI agent This mirrors how OpenClaw works You can send text messages to Claude from your phone - and receive back notifications It turns your terminal-based AI agent (Claude Code) into an "always-on" assistant that you can "text" with A "Channel" is technically a specialized Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. It acts as a two-way bridge between an external service and your active Claude Code session Inbound: When you send a message via Telegram or Discord, it is pushed into the active Claude Code session as an event.Outbound: Claude can use its internal tools to execute commands, fix bugs, or run tests, and then reply back to you through that same message thread /plugin install telegram@claude-plugins-official /telegram:configure <your_bot_token> claude --channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official Pairing: Send a message to your bot; it will give you a code to enter in the terminal to verify your identity

slides.title: Anthropic Claude Cowork Projects Claude Cowork Projects https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4CiCwvAA5FI
slides.text: Anthropic Claude Cowork Projects Claude Cowork Projects https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4CiCwvAA5FI Projects function as dedicated workspaces with their own files, persistent memory, instructions, skills, and scheduled tasks Example - using projects for specific business areas like YouTube content creation, where Claude remembers brand voice, upload schedules, and performs automated competitor analysis Projects can be enhanced with memory features, web connectors, and integration with other apps. Claude vs OpenClaw Anthropic recently added Claude features which closely mirror OpenClaw  - persistent desktop automation, computer use (navigating apps and browsers like a human), mobile task delegation via the Claude app, and integrations with Slack, Google Workspace, and Notion - all without complex setup. This covers 90% of his OpenClaw use cases with far less security risk OpenClaw remains relevant: it's free, open-source, works with any LLM, runs on Linux/Mac/Windows, and builds deep personalized memory Claude's version is sandboxed, beginner-friendly, and Mac-only for now - a safer but less flexible alternative Claude Code "Auto-Mode" setting A built-in "classifier" robot checks every action before Claude executes it - and blocks only "unsafe" operations . Thus user doesn't have to "approve" dozens of times. And it is safer than the old "skip permissions" mode Toggle "Allow auto permissions mode" in settings, and run the command claude enable auto mode in the terminal Currently available for Claude Team Plan users, with Enterprise and API access rolling out shortly after Remote Control - for Claude Code Dispatch - for Claude Cowork Desktop app 3 Claude Code Hacks: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/tQuinn9FpMA /hook I want you to create a sound when you finish a task /statusline create status line to include ... /skill-creator create a skill that humanizes AI-generated text

slides.title: Claude Desktop Computer Use Anthropic's computer use feature
slides.text: Claude Desktop Computer Use Anthropic's computer use feature It makes screen snapshots - and controls keyboard and mouse to take over browser and applications Anthropic has a "block list" for certain actions in the browser implemented for major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). The workaround is to use a less popular light weight open source browser (like "Min Browser" - minbrowser.org ) which is not on Anthropic's block list Once Claude's computer use is enabled in Claude Desktop's settings (under General → Browser Use + Computer Use), you direct it via the Co-work tab by prepending requests with "computer use." Claude then opens Min Browser, where a yellow outline visually confirms it has taken control. It operates by taking rapid screenshots and then physically moving your mouse and typing via your keyboard — mimicking genuine human interaction You can intervene at any time to make minor adjustments without breaking the workflow This human-like behavior is exactly what bypasses bot-detection on platforms like LinkedIn, Instagram, and Facebook, which normally block traditional browser automation scripts. Min Browser Min Browser - open source, not blocked by Claude https://minbrowser.org https://github.com/minbrowser/min https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2u93VTYvG5U The core difference is that Anthropic intentionally restricts Chrome (and Safari, Firefox, Edge) from performing outreach-style write actions - like sending LinkedIn connection requests or filling out forms. The Claude Chrome extension enables some browser control, but it won't let you do the automation tasks shown in the video. Min Browser bypasses that restriction entirely, giving Claude unrestricted read and write access

slides.title: Anthropic vs US Government On March 24, 2026,
slides.text: Anthropic vs US Government On March 24, 2026, a federal judge in San Francisco heard Anthropic's request to block the Pentagon's "supply chain risk" blacklisting of the company On March 25 Judge Rita Lin issued a 43-page preliminary injunction ruling in Anthropic's favor. She blocked the Trump administration from enforcing the presidential directive banning federal agencies from using Claude, and halted the Pentagon's "supply chain risk" designation. She wrote that "there is nothing in the relevant statute that supports the dystopian idea that a U.S. company can be labeled as a potential enemy and saboteur for dissenting with the government" The ruling is not yet in full effect - Judge Lin put it on hold for one week to give the Justice Department time to appeal Claude Mythos - Anthropic's most powerful AI model yet, accidentally leaked on March 26, 2026 due to a misconfigured data cache It introduces a new top-tier model tier called Capybara, surpassing Opus It dramatically outperforms previous Claude models in coding, reasoning, and cybersecurity benchmarks It's currently in limited early access, restricted to cyber defense organizations, with no public release date announced https://fortune.com/2026/03/27/anthropic-data-leak-reveals-powerful-secret-mythos-ai-model/

slides.title: Tesla TeraFab Tesla TeraFab Tesla has been designing
slides.text: Tesla TeraFab Tesla TeraFab Tesla has been designing its own AI inference chips for Full Self-Driving (FSD) since 2019, when it transitioned away from NVIDIA hardware The FSD Chip are custom-built to run Tesla's neural networks for autonomous driving Tesla has historically relied on TSMC and Samsung to manufacture them - but this will change with the new TeraFab TeraFab will be built at Tesla's facility in Austin, Texas. Planned investment $20-25 Bln. The facility will do logic, packaging, testing, lithography mask production, and chip evaluation all under one roof. TeraFab will produce two chip variants: Edge inference chips - for cars and robots Space-hardened chips - for SpaceX satellites Musk targets a staggering output of 100–200 GW of terrestrial AI compute per year, with up to 1 terawatt** destined for space-based AI on solar-powered satellites. For context, the entire global AI compute output today is roughly 20 gigawatts. https://www.investors.com/news/tesla-stock-elon-musk-tesla-spacex-terafab-project/

slides.text: TradingAgents TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework Open Source, from US (UCLA/Los Angeles project) https://tradingagents-ai.github.io/ https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.20138 https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents https://x.com/heynavtoor/status/2035199111872618555 TradingAgents is utilizing multiple LLM-powered agents with specialized roles such as fundamental, sentiment, and technical analysts, as well as traders with diverse risk profiles The system features Bull and Bear researchers evaluating market conditions, a risk management team overseeing exposure, and traders integrating insights from debates and historical data to make informed decisions This collaborative, dynamic environment enhances trading performance, as demonstrated by our comprehensive experiments showing significant improvements in cumulative returns, Sharpe ratio, and maximum drawdown compared to baseline models Our results highlight the effectiveness of multi-agent LLM frameworks in financial trading .

slides.title: AI on Databricks platform Mosaic AI - full
slides.text: AI on Databricks platform Mosaic AI - full AI lifecycle - from data prep to model deployment Building, evaluating, deploying, and monitoring AI applications, whether you're using open-source models, fine-tuned LLMs, or external APIs https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/ AI/BI Genie - query data using text prompts (no SQL or Python) Genie Agent Mode - automatically generates and executes multi-step research plans, tests hypotheses, and delivers comprehensive answers with tables and charts Databricks One - UI for multi-agent chat experience powered by Genie AI Functions - built-in SQL functions that apply AI models directly to your data in notebooks, Databricks SQL, Lakeflow pipelines, and Workflows. Examples - ai_analyze_sentiment, ai_classify, ai_extract, ai_fix_grammar, ai_gen, ai_query() - call any model (foundation models, external LLMs, or your own custom ML models ) Mosaic AI Agent Framework - build, test, and deploy autonomous agents that can reason over tasks, use tools, and work with your organization's data in a governed environment: Model Serving (REST endpoints), AI Gateway with usage tracking, payload logging, and rate limiting; External Models APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) RAG & Vector Search Data Governance with Unity Catalog - control plane for all data, models, agents, and AI assets across clouds. It enforces access control, auditing, and data lineage — critical when using sensitive enterprise data with AI applications and staying compliant with GDPR and HIPAA

slides.title: Google Stitch - Free AI UI Vibe Design
slides.text: Google Stitch - Free AI UI Vibe Design Google Stitch - Free AI UI Vibe Design https://stitch.withgoogle.com Accepts natural language prompts, hand-drawn sketches, or screenshots into high-fidelity web and mobile interface designs Rapid prototyping UIs, Powered by Google's Gemini May 2025 - first intro, Dec 2025 - major update March 17–18, 2026 - update transformed Stitch into a full "AI-native design canvas", introducing a complete UI redesign with new features https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/stitch-ai-ui-design/ Infinite AI-native canvas - text, images, and code New design agent + Agent Manager - reasons across an entire project's history and lets you run multiple design directions in parallel DESIGN.md - an agent-friendly markdown file for exporting / importing design systems to/from other tools, including coding tools Interactive prototypes - stitch screens together and click "Play" to instantly preview app flows; AI auto-generates logical next screens Voice control - speak to canvas for real-time critiques and design updates MCP server & SDK - lets Stitch connect to developer tools like AI Studio for seamless design-to-code handoffs Figma remains the gold standard for production-level work requiring fine-grained control, team collaboration, and developer handoff Tools like v0 and Bolt.new sit closer to the code side, while Stitch bridges design and code without requiring deep expertise in either Stitch's biggest limitation remains its tendency to default to Material Design components, making it less ideal for iOS-focused products.

slides.title: Boston Dynamics Robots for Manufacturing Why Boston Dynamics'
slides.text: Boston Dynamics Robots for Manufacturing Why Boston Dynamics' New Atlas is Years Ahead of Tesla https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ll784fIsQew History of financing: Google - viewed it as a software platform, no hardware infrastructure SoftBank - teated it as a financial investment/IPO play Hyundai - realized that the most expensive parts of a robot, actuators, are 60% similar to automotive electric power steering units. Since Hyundai already produces these by the millions, they could scale production and ensure reliability in a way a tech company or investment firm never could The new electric Atlas (replacing the old hydraulic version) is designed for the "human world" but with superhuman capabilities: 360-Degree Movement Industrial Strength, water and dust resistant, can operate from -4 to 104°F; Endless Operation - robot can swap its own battery in 3 minutes without human help Uses Google DeepMind’s Gemini for logic language, and Toyota Research Institute tech for "one-shot" learning Aiming for a higher price ($200K) - but reliability, no mistakes, 24/7 operations, 10 years durability The 2026 production run is already sold out at $200K/unit Hyundai is investing $26 Bln into U.S. manufacturing, including a dedicated factory aiming to produce 30K units per year by 2030. Tesla focuses on a "robot for every home," at $20K price

slides.text: Misc AI Updates Perplexity Health - integrates with Apple Health (iPhone and iPad) and platforms including Fitbit, Ultrahuman, Withings, and Clue. Health data is not used to train AI models or sold to third parties OpenAI announced a $110 Bln funding round at a $840 Bln post-money valuation (50-Amazon, 30-Nvidia, 30-Softbank) on Feb 26–27. The round remains open. This is the largest ever private tech fundraise. DeepSeek's Engram - Conditional Memory for Transformers Engram is a new architectural block that adds conditional memory to transformers, sitting alongside traditional attention and feedforward layers Instead of recomputing familiar multi-token phrases at runtime, Engram acts like a lookup table, recognizing common patterns and instantly retrieving pre-stored representations via hash-based lookups with contextualized gating Studies show models reach final predictions earlier in the network, ffectively gaining functional depth without adding layers

slides.title: AI Misc Anthropic AutoDream feature for Claude that
slides.text: AI Misc Anthropic AutoDream feature for Claude that automatically consolidates and cleans memory files using a background sub-agent https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LrgfmZkl3nc AutoDream periodically reviews chat sessions, prunes unnecessary information, and organizes memory files to reduce bloat and improve recall The feature runs automatically based on time intervals or session counts, touching only memory files while leaving code untouched. Users can enable it through the /memory interface and manually trigger it with /dream feature command (Piebald) "Hey, I want to create a new skill. I want it called dream. Use this to build it. ...". AutoDream works alongside existing auto-memory features to create a three-layer memory system that maintains cleaner, more focused context across sessions, reducing repetition and making Claude feel more like a human assistant with organized long-term memory rather than a forgetful chatbot. Screen Pipe - free open-source AI memory works with Claude Code Records screen and audio locally https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8eustEguF9Q The tool analyzes what you're working on, tracks time spent on tasks, and recommends high-value, low-effort automations tailored to your specific needs Piebald /dream feature command https://piebald.ai https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2chQzrrGfUw https://github.com/Piebald-AI https://github.com/Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts https://github.com/Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts/blob/main/system-prompts/agent-prompt-dream-memory-consolidation.md

slides.title: Meta's Hyperagents - Self-modification Meta's Hyperagents are a
slides.text: Meta's Hyperagents - Self-modification Meta's Hyperagents are a new class of self-referential AI systems introduced by researchers from FAIR at Meta and Meta Superintelligence Labs (alongside academic partners) in March 2026 Built as an extension of the Darwin Gödel Machine, they enable metacognitive self-modification - meaning they don't just improve at tasks, they also rewrite the very process that generates those improvements The meta-level mechanism is fully editable, not fixed Tested across coding, paper review, robotics reward design, and Olympiad-level math grading, Hyperagents achieved transferable performance gains where prior systems scored zero OpenClaw Nerve Dashboard It replaces complex terminal setups with a clean, user-friendly dashboard that features a Trello-like Kanban board for task organization, a file manager, and a proposal inbox where users can approve agent actions Key highlights include a voice mode powered by Whisper, the ability to easily manage fleets of sub-agents with specific models and "thinking levels", and real-time editing of agent memory and context. Installation is quick, requiring only a GitHub link to be pasted into the OpenClaw gateway https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mGFlD40FFwM

slides.title: Misc Claude AI + Obsidian = Your Own
slides.text: Misc Claude AI + Obsidian = Your Own JARVIS https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UHLagfG2nJE Obsidian stores all your notes, research, and business information locally on your computer as plain text files, while Claude can access this entire knowledge base for context-aware responses. The setup involves creating an Obsidian vault, organizing folders for clients/projects, installing Claude Code, and creating a "Claude.md" briefing file. This creates continuity between sessions, allowing Claude to understand your business, remember previous work, and provide more relevant outputs. The system costs around $20 monthly and becomes more powerful over time as you add more information, essentially creating a knowledgeable AI assistant that knows your specific context and work. Hermes Agent by News Research https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d7TABYDHSE8 Hermes Agent has a self-improving capability - it learns and remembers from each interaction, building a skill library based on user preferences and work patterns Hermes stores experiences as searchable markdown files, becoming more personalized over time like a trained AI employee Hermes has 8,800 GitHub stars Hermes runs on multiple platforms, integrates with messaging apps, and can operate 24/7 on a $5 server Claude + Collaborator https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RJWbk-4JvLU Collaborator is a free Mac desktop app that allows you to run multiple AI agent teams, particularly Claude instances, working together on a single project through an organized canvas interface The app lets you open different terminals where each Claude agent can focus on specific tasks like UI improvement, design, or copywriting, all within the same project folder. Unlike using regular terminals which can be messy, Collaborator provides a clean dashboard where you can orchestrate multiple agents simultaneously and see their work in real-time through live previews. The app also supports browser tiles for web browsing and can potentially work with other AI models like OpenClaw.

slides.text: LightLLM Compromize On March 24, 2026, a threat actor group called TeamPCP (linked to LAPSUS$) compromised two LiteLLM PyPI releases — v1.82.7 and v1.82.8 — by injecting malicious code into the distributed Python wheel packages LiteLLM is an open-source Python library and proxy server that acts as a "universal translator" normalizing APIs of LLM providers into the familiar OpenAI API format LiteLLM has over 95 Mln monthly downloads The affected file - litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py It installs a hidden systemd backdoor that survived reboots and polled an attacker-controlled server for additional payloads How to check if you have it: uv pip show litellm find ~/.cache -name "litellm_init.pth" 2>/dev/null ls ~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py 2>/dev/null ls ~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service 2>/dev/null cat ~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py 2>/dev/null find ~/.cache/pip ~/.cache/uv -name "litellm*.whl" 2>/dev/null
